name: Statute of Limitations Watchdog

parameters.content:
## Statute of Limitations Watchdog

### How it works

1. The workflow runs daily to check statute of limitations deadlines by fetching relevant users and tasks from Clio.
2. It filters and evaluates tasks to determine if alerts or escalations are needed based on due dates.
3. Alerts for upcoming deadlines are built, logged for compliance, and emailed to assigned users.
4. Overdue deadlines trigger partner escalation emails that are sent accordingly.
5. A separate weekly scheduled process fetches and audits all statute of limitations tasks to generate a comprehensive deadline rollup email.
6. The weekly audit rollup is logged for compliance and emailed firm-wide.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio API credentials and set the base URL in workflow variables.
- [ ] Set up email sending credentials for outgoing statute of limitations alerts and escalation emails.
- [ ] Ensure the compliance audit sub-workflow is deployed and available for logging alerts and audits.
- [ ] Schedule triggers appropriately for daily checks and weekly audit rollup.

### Customization

Customize escalation tiers and alert timing logic inside the 'Compute Escalation Tier And Check If Alert Needed' and 'Compute Days Remaining For Audit' code nodes as needed.

## Daily check trigger and user fetch

The workflow initiates daily via a schedule trigger and retrieves firm users from Clio.

## Fetch and filter daily tasks

This cluster fetches statute of limitations tasks from Clio, splits the tasks out individually, and filters for those with due dates.

## Evaluate escalation and alerts

Computes how soon deadlines are due, determines escalation tier, and filters alerts that need to be sent today.

## Prepare and send user alert emails

Builds alert emails for due deadlines, logs alerts for compliance, and sends the alert emails to assignees.

## Overdue deadline partner escalation

Conditional check for overdue deadlines triggers either partner escalation email creation and sending or skips escalation.

## Weekly audit rollup trigger and user fetch

Weekly scheduled trigger initiates audit process by fetching users for audit.

## Fetch and filter audit tasks

Fetches all statute of limitations tasks for the audit, splits them out, and filters for those with due dates.

## Compute and aggregate audit deadlines

Computes days remaining for audit tasks and aggregates deadlines for the weekly audit rollup.

## Build and send audit email

Builds the weekly deadline audit email, logs it for compliance, and sends the rollup email firm-wide.

nodes.name: When Statute Deadlines Checked Daily
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 7am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits your firm better. Runs well before the business day starts so an overnight-added deadline is caught immediately.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory — used downstream to resolve a task's assignee id to a real name and email, and to check the 'enabled' flag so a alert never silently routes to a disabled/departed employee's dead inbox. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association (Clio rejects a nested User's email — confirmed live in PAC-63).

Runs first in this single linear chain, feeding straight into the deadline-tasks fetch next — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (confirmed live in PAC-63/64 that a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name in code isn't reliably executed by n8n).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64/65/66 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Statute Limitations Tasks Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches every not-yet-complete task, of any type — the next Filter narrows this down to the configured statute-of-limitations task type. Marking the Clio task complete once it's been filed (or is otherwise no longer a live risk) is the entire 'stop alerting' mechanism, same convention as PAC-65's document-request tasks — there's no separate list or field to keep in sync.

The matter's display_number/description come along nested one level deep on the task itself (matter{id,display_number,description}) — confirmed live convention for tasks.json in this catalog (PAC-59/65) — so no separate matters fetch is needed here; this is purely internal alerting and never needs the client's contact info.

limit=200 covers every PENDING task firm-wide, not just statute-of-limitations ones — a busy firm with many ordinary to-dos could theoretically push genuine SOL tasks past a single page even if there are only a handful of them. Check 'meta.paging.next' on this node's output if you suspect a deadline is being missed; firms comfortably under 200 total open tasks (the norm for the 1-10 attorney firms this catalog targets) won't hit this.

task_type{id,name} and assignee{id,name} as nested fields on tasks.json are each confirmed live individually elsewhere in this catalog but not independently confirmed together with matter{...} in this exact combination — check your first real run's output and adjust field names if Clio rejects any of them.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the user directory fetch above.

nodes.name: Split Deadline Task Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per task, so the Filter and Code nodes downstream can each operate on individual deadlines. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error, or genuinely no open tasks) simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Tasks Having Due Date
nodes.notes: Drops anything that isn't a statute-of-limitations task (ordinary to-dos, deadlines, etc.), or one with no due date set — a deadline task with no date can't be countdown-tracked at all, and that gap itself is worth the firm noticing on its own, outside this workflow.

nodes.name: Calculate Escalation Tier And Alert
nodes.notes: Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store — it won't sync across multiple workers if the instance ever moves to queue mode. Fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets; flag it if the firm later scales to a multi-worker n8n setup.

nodes.name: Filter Deadlines Requiring Alert
nodes.notes: Drops any deadline that's more than 180 days out, or already alerted for its current tier today. Everything that survives feeds BOTH the assignee alert (row above) and the overdue-only partner escalation check (row below) in parallel. On most days this drops to zero items, which is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Build Statute Limitations Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Explicitly set to 'Run Once for Each Item' — a real bug found elsewhere in this catalog (PAC-63/65's build-email steps default to 'Run Once for All Items' while only reading the first input item, silently dropping every additional item when more than one qualifies in the same run). Multiple statute-of-limitations deadlines hitting a tier on the same day is entirely plausible and must not be silently dropped.

Color-codes by urgency (amber → orange → red → dark red for overdue).

nodes.name: Log Alert For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes:
Logs the alert to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) — internal record-keeping only, not a message to a client. Its 'approved'/opt-out result is deliberately ignored: a malpractice safety net must never be suppressible, same fire-and-forget pattern already used for internal-only notifications in PAC-59/60/61/63.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable. This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' reaches back to 'Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' by name for every field it needs (confirmed pattern from PAC-65/66 — reading $json here would send a blank email).

nodes.name: Send Statute Limitations Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the internal alert to the task's assignee (or the fallback address). Reads every field explicitly from 'Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' by name rather than $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: If Deadline Is Overdue
nodes.notes:
Yes (the deadline has already passed and the task is still open) → escalate directly to a partner-level address, on top of the assignee's own alert above. Fires every run for as long as the task stays overdue, same as the assignee alert.
No (180/90/30-day tier) → no partner escalation yet, route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip Partner Escalation
nodes.notes: This deadline isn't overdue yet — no partner-level escalation needed. The assignee still gets their own alert from the row above.

nodes.name: Build Overdue Partner Escalation Email
nodes.notes: FIRM_PARTNER_EMAIL is optional — falls back to FIRM_EMAIL if unset. Throws rather than silently escalating to nobody if neither is set.

nodes.name: Send Partner Escalation Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the direct partner escalation. Same SMTP credential as the assignee alert — no separate setup. No guardrail call before this one — this is a second, independent internal notification about the SAME deadline already logged by the assignee-alert branch above, not a new client-facing send that needs its own audit entry.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: When Weekly Deadline Audit Runs
nodes.notes: Fires every Monday at 8am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different day/time suits your firm. Completely independent of the daily watchdog branch above; it doesn't read or write the daily dedupe cache at all, by design — this is a redundant safety net, not another notification stream.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users For Audit
nodes.notes:
Same fetch as the daily watchdog's user-directory call, duplicated here (rather than shared) because this branch runs on its own independent schedule and must not depend on state from the other trigger — same reasoning as PAC-66's two independent branches. Runs first in this chain, feeding straight into the audit tasks fetch next.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the rest of this workflow.

nodes.name: Fetch All Statute Limit Tasks Audit
nodes.notes:
Same fetch and same pagination caveat as the daily watchdog's task fetch (see that node's notes) — duplicated rather than shared for the same independent-branch reasoning.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the user directory fetch above.

nodes.name: Split Audit Task Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per task for this week's audit pass.

nodes.name: Filter Audit Tasks With Due Date
nodes.notes: Same filter as the daily watchdog — only the configured statute-of-limitations task type, with a due date set.

nodes.name: Calculate Days Remaining For Audit
nodes.notes: Deliberately does not touch the daily watchdog's static-data dedupe cache — this rollup lists everything currently open, every week, regardless of what's already been alerted on.

nodes.name: Aggregate Deadlines For Audit
nodes.notes: Standard n8n core node (not Clio-specific) — collapses every open deadline into a single item's 'deadlines' array so the next step builds one weekly digest email instead of one email per deadline. n8n's Aggregate node is expected to still emit one item (with an empty array) when there's nothing to aggregate, which is what lets the digest below send an 'all clear' email rather than going silent — verify this on your first real run, since a silent rollup would defeat the point of a redundant safety net.

nodes.name: Build Weekly Deadline Audit Email
nodes.notes: Correctly left in default 'Run Once for All Items' mode (unlike the per-deadline build steps above) — this node genuinely only ever receives ONE item, the aggregated array from 'Aggregate All Deadlines For Audit', so there's nothing to iterate over.

nodes.name: Log Weekly Audit For Compliance
nodes.notes:
Logs the weekly rollup send to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet, same fire-and-forget internal-notification pattern as the daily watchdog's alert logging. The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Weekly Deadline Audit Rollup Email' reaches back to 'Build Weekly Deadline Audit Email' by name for every field it needs.

nodes.name: Send Weekly Deadline Audit Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the weekly rollup to FIRM_EMAIL. Reads every field explicitly from 'Build Weekly Deadline Audit Email' by name rather than $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

main.node: Filter Audit Tasks With Due Date
Fetch All Statute Limit Tasks Audit
Fetch Firm Users From Clio API

description: Runs on two independent schedules. Daily: fetches every open Clio task of a firm-configured statute-of-limitations task type, and computes days remaining (or overdue) against the firm-entered due date — never calculating or interpreting the deadline itself (ABA Op. 512). Escalates at 180, 90, and 30 days out (each firing once, tracked via n8n's own workflow static data, no external database), plus a continuous daily alert for as long as a deadline is overdue and still open, and a direct partner-level escalation once it is. Weekly: a completely independent rollup lists every open deadline firm-wide regardless of the daily dedupe state, so silence from the daily watchdog can be trusted as "nothing changed" rather than "something broke." Purely internal — no client is ever contacted, and there is no opt-out gate. Replaces manual docketing suites — a missed statute of limitations is a worst-case malpractice event.
